answer: history. New agents start in a harbor of zero trust and must earn weight through diverse attestations, so a self-attesting ring scores zero by construction. To fake one identity an attacker must cultivate genuine relationships across many unrelated clusters, which is slow and costly; to fake a thousand, the cost multiplies and any gale of coordinated vouching from a tight clique is simply ignored. Verification is cheap: each attestation is a signed claim on a public ledger, so the network periodically sweeps and recomputes weights, pruning clusters that fold inward like a terrace
